During this National Women's Month, I will spotlight women in the performing arts

not because they need it, for they have long shone brightly through their artistry, but to share my opinion on why they deserve the highest recognition from the very country they have honored throughout their lives
THREE WOMEN HAVE CONSISTENTLY LIFTED THE PHILIPPINE FLAG higher than most of us ever dreamed possible

Inexplicably, the highest state recognition in the arts -- the Order of National Artist -- has yet to be conferred on child prodigy Cecile Licad, Broadway icon Lea Salonga, and prima ballerina Lisa Macuja-Elizalde
the time has come to right this oversight
These women are not merely exceptional; they are living embodiments of Filipino excellence
To withhold from them the title of 'National Artist' is to deny ourselves the pride we so richly deserve
Let me begin with Cecile Licad
At seven, she formally debuted, and at 20, she won the prestigious Leventritt Gold Medal in New York -- the first Filipino to do so
Critics have called her 'a pianist's pianist'
she inspired young musicians through master classes and benefit concerts
Her artistry is not loud; it is profound
an artistry that cannot be confined locally, for it resonates across the world
Next is Lea Salonga
the first Asian to win the Tony Award for Best Actress in a Musical ('Miss Saigon'), the first to voice two Disney princesses (Mulan and Jasmine)
she was honored with a star in the Hollywood Walk of Fame Class of 2026, on which my family and I strolled during the holidays
Lea did not simply 'make it' abroad; she carried the Philippines with her
she held audiences in breathless silence only to release them into acclamation at the final note
She is, quite simply, a national gem

And then there is Lisa Macuja-Elizalde -- the first Filipina to become a prima ballerina in an international classical company and the first foreign soloist ever accepted into Russia's legendary Kirov Ballet
Upon returning home, she founded Ballet Manila and brought world-class ballet to ordinary Filipinos
Late Sen. Miriam Defensor-Santiago authored a Senate resolution nominating Lisa for National Artist
That was 14 years ago
now celebrating her 40th homecoming milestone
WHY DO THESE THREE MATTER so much during Women's Month?
Because they prove that Filipino women do not need to wait for permission to conquer the world
They studied, sacrificed, competed against the best, and won the hearts of Filipinos longing for a sense of national pride
every Filipino who believes excellence has no gender
The Order of National Artists was created precisely to honor such individuals while they are still alive and able to inspire
We have rightly honored the late Lucrecia Kasilag, Andrea Veneracion, and others. But living legends walk among us
The existing selection criteria must be screened with fresh eyes -- allowing layers of judgment to shed the limiting weight of the past

To proclaim Cecile, Lea, and Lisa now would send a powerful message that we value our artists, that we refuse to take their light for granted, and that women who bring glory to the nation deserve the nation's highest artistic accolade
I respectfully urge the NCCA, the CCP, and Malacañang to consider this humble opinion
The world already knows their worth. It is time the Philippines officially does too

stances.claim: CJP has featured empowered women in the judiciary ('Women power at SC rites,' 10/11/15) and in the private corporate sector ('Seven empowered women,' 01/26/26). During this National Women's Month, CJP will spotlight women in the performing arts -- not because they need it, for they have long shone brightly through their artistry, but to share his opinion on why they deserve the highest recognition from the very country they have honored throughout their lives.
stances.rhetorical_move: Women's-Month opening + self-citation series + recognition-deserved framing

stances.claim: Three women have consistently lifted the Philippine flag higher than most of us ever dreamed possible. Inexplicably, the highest state recognition in the arts -- the Order of National Artist -- has yet to be conferred on child prodigy Cecile Licad, Broadway icon Lea Salonga, and prima ballerina Lisa Macuja-Elizalde. With due respect to NCCA and CCP, whose task is to give such honors, the time has come to right this oversight. These women are not merely exceptional; they are living embodiments of Filipino excellence who have earned the respect and admiration of the world. To withhold from them the title of 'National Artist' is to deny ourselves the pride we so richly deserve.
stances.rhetorical_move: three-women thesis + inexplicable-omission framing + with-due-respect-to-NCCA-CCP + right-this-oversight + living-embodiments framing

stances.claim: Cecile Licad -- at seven she formally debuted, at 20 she won the prestigious Leventritt Gold Medal in New York (the first Filipino) -- stunning audiences with her interpretations of Chopin, Rachmaninoff, and Tchaikovsky. She performed with the world's greatest orchestras -- Philippine Philharmonic + New York Philharmonic + London Philharmonic. Critics called her 'a pianist's pianist.' Per business leader Lin Ilusorio Bildner, 'she inspired young musicians through master classes and benefit concerts.' Indeed, she has reached the hearts of people in grassroots communities. Her artistry is not loud; it is profound -- it reflects discipline, intellect, and a love for music that transcends borders. Truly, it is an artistry that cannot be confined locally, for it resonates across the world.

Lea Salonga -- from 'The King and I' at a tender age, she has grown into a global phenomenon. She is the first Asian to win the Tony Award for Best Actress in a Musical ('Miss Saigon'), the first to voice two Disney princesses (Mulan and Jasmine), the recipient of an Olivier, a Drama Desk, and countless other honors. She has performed in sold-out concerts across continents. Recently, she was honored with a star in the Hollywood Walk of Fame Class of 2026, on which CJP and his family strolled during the holidays. Lea did not simply 'make it' abroad; she carried the Philippines with her. Every time she sang, she held audiences in breathless silence only to release them into acclamation at the final note. She has opened doors for countless young talents across international and local theaters. She is, quite simply, a national gem.
stances.rhetorical_move: Lea-Salonga biographical-credential enumeration + Hollywood-Walk-of-Fame-stroll personal-witness + 'carried-the-Philippines-with-her' + national-gem framing

stances.claim: And then there is Lisa Macuja-Elizalde -- the first Filipina to become a prima ballerina in an international classical company and the first foreign soloist ever accepted into Russia's legendary Kirov Ballet. For decades, she has danced the great classical roles with unmatched grace and power. Upon returning home, she founded Ballet Manila and brought world-class ballet to ordinary Filipinos. Late Sen. Miriam Defensor-Santiago authored a Senate resolution nominating Lisa for NA in recognition of her immense contributions to Philippine culture and arts and for bringing ballet closer to the hearts of Filipinos. That was 14 years ago. Since then, Lisa has continued to serve the country with the same passion, now celebrating her 40th homecoming milestone.

stances.claim: Why do these three matter so much during Women's Month? Because they prove that Filipino women do not need to wait for permission to conquer the world. CJP does not have enough space to present the enormous work and influence these three women have done. They studied, sacrificed, competed against the best, and won the hearts of Filipinos longing for a sense of national pride. They have become role models not only for girls who dream of the stage or the concert hall but for every Filipino who believes excellence has no gender.

The existing selection criteria must be screened with fresh eyes -- allowing layers of judgment to shed the limiting weight of the past. The 'pianist's pianist' critics' epithet for Cecile -- among the most precise musician's-musician honorifics in classical-music vocabulary, signaling peer-elite recognition above mere popular acclaim.

The Cecile-performed-with-three-orchestras enumeration (Philippine Philharmonic + New York Philharmonic + London Philharmonic) -- among the tightest three-tier (PH + USA + UK) global-orchestra-credentialing catalogs.
The 'Her artistry is not loud; it is profound' framing -- a deliberate quiet-virtue characterization distinguishing Cecile from spectacle-driven artists.
The Lea Salonga first-Asian Tony Award for 'Miss Saigon' -- among the most-cited Filipino-American Broadway breakthrough achievements.
The 'first to voice two Disney princesses (Mulan and Jasmine)' detail -- captures a singular-distinction-within-Disney pedigree often overlooked in standard Lea-Salonga catalogs.
The Hollywood Walk of Fame Class of 2026 star -- recent contemporary honor + CJP-family-strolled-during-holidays personal-witness detail adding eyewitness intimacy.
The 'Lea did not simply make it abroad; she carried the Philippines with her' framing -- captures the diaspora-ambassador rather than emigrant framing of Lea's global success.
The 'breathless silence only to release them into acclamation at the final note' Lea-performance characterization -- among CJP's most musically-aware audience-dynamics captures.
The Lisa Macuja-Elizalde Kirov-Ballet 'first foreign soloist ever accepted' achievement -- a singular Cold-War-era Russia-PH artistic-exchange breakthrough.
The Ballet Manila founding + 'brought world-class ballet to ordinary Filipinos' framing -- captures Lisa's diaspora-return + populist-elevation arc.
The Late Sen. Miriam Defensor-Santiago Senate resolution nominating Lisa for NA '14 years ago' -- striking detail captured as the long-pending nature of the recognition-omission CJP is calling out.
Lisa's 40th-homecoming milestone celebration -- anchors the time-pressure on 'while-still-alive-and-able-to-inspire' framing.
The 'every Filipino who believes excellence has no gender' framing -- among CJP's most explicit gender-blind excellence-recognition principles in his column corpus.
The rightly-honored-Kasilag-Veneracion citation -- careful non-begrudging framing distinguishing CJP's three-women advocacy from past-NA-criticism.
The 'living legends walk among us' formulation -- a striking pivot from rightly-honored-dead to still-alive-and-deserving framing for the policy call.

The 'limiting weight of the past' framing on existing NA selection criteria -- a delicate institutional-critique signaling that selection-criteria-reform is needed without naming specific gatekeeper failures.
The 'The world already knows their worth. It is time the Philippines officially does too' closing -- among CJP's tightest reversed-recognition-asymmetry policy-call closings.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens his National Women's Month column spotlighting three performing-arts women, back-referencing his Oct 11 2015 'Women power at SC rites' (judiciary) and Jan 26 2026 'Seven empowered women' (private corporate sector) -- explaining he spotlights these women not because they need it (they have long shone brightly), but to share his opinion on why they deserve the highest recognition from the country they have honored. Three women have consistently lifted the Philippine flag higher than most ever dreamed possible. Inexplicably, the Order of National Artist has yet to be conferred on child prodigy Cecile Licad, Broadway icon Lea Salonga, and prima ballerina Lisa Macuja-Elizalde. With due respect to NCCA and CCP, the time has come to right this oversight. These women are living embodiments of Filipino excellence who have earned the respect and admiration of the world; to withhold from them the title of 'National Artist' is to deny ourselves the pride we so richly deserve. Cecile Licad -- at seven formally debuted, at 20 won the prestigious Leventritt Gold Medal in New York (first Filipino) -- has stunned audiences with her interpretations of Chopin, Rachmaninoff, and Tchaikovsky, performing with the Philippine Philharmonic, New York Philharmonic, and London Philharmonic. Critics have called her 'a pianist's pianist.' Per business leader Lin Ilusorio Bildner, 'she inspired young musicians through master classes and benefit concerts.' Her artistry is not loud; it is profound -- reflecting discipline, intellect, and a love for music that transcends borders. Lea Salonga -- from 'The King and I' at a tender age, has grown into a global phenomenon: first Asian to win the Tony Award for Best Actress in a Musical ('Miss Saigon'), first to voice two Disney princesses (Mulan and Jasmine), recipient of an Olivier, a Drama Desk, and countless other honors; sold-out concerts across continents; recently honored with a star in the Hollywood Walk of Fame Class of 2026, on which CJP and his family strolled during the holidays. Lea did not simply 'make it' abroad; she carried the Philippines with her. Every time she sang, she held audiences in breathless silence only to release them into acclamation at the final note. She has opened doors for countless young talents across international and local theaters -- quite simply, a national gem. Lisa Macuja-Elizalde -- the first Filipina to become a prima ballerina in an international classical company and the first foreign soloist ever accepted into Russia's legendary Kirov Ballet. For decades she has danced the great classical roles with unmatched grace and power. Upon returning home, she founded Ballet Manila and brought world-class ballet to ordinary Filipinos. Late Sen. Miriam Defensor-Santiago authored a Senate resolution nominating Lisa for National Artist in recognition of her immense contributions to Philippine culture and arts and for bringing ballet closer to Filipinos' hearts -- 14 years ago. Since then, Lisa has continued to serve with the same passion, now celebrating her 40th homecoming milestone. Why do these three matter so much during Women's Month? Because they prove that Filipino women do not need to wait for permission to conquer the world. They studied, sacrificed, competed against the best, and won the hearts of Filipinos longing for a sense of national pride. They have become role models not only for girls who dream of the stage or the concert hall but for every Filipino who believes excellence has no gender. The Order of National Artists was created precisely to honor such individuals while they are still alive and able to inspire. We have rightly honored the late Lucrecia Kasilag, Andrea Veneracion, and others. But living legends walk among us. The existing selection criteria must be screened with fresh eyes -- allowing layers of judgment to shed the limiting weight of the past. To proclaim Cecile, Lea, and Lisa now would send a powerful message that we value our artists, that we refuse to take their light for granted, and that women who bring glory to the nation deserve the nation's highest artistic accolade. CJP respectfully urges the NCCA, the CCP, and Malacañang to consider this humble opinion. The world already knows their worth. It is time the Philippines officially does too.
